calls.reason: In 2022 tests, GPT-3 addition broke down when the numbers were simply reformatted (MIT CSAIL). A 2022 preprint found GPT-3 failed copy and addition outside its examples unless given outside help. Both point to incomplete rule mastery.

OpenAI's note that ChatGPT gives plausible wrong answers and HELM's partial knowledge scores are too thin. No test checks whether the launch-era model tells valid entity-property pairings from invalid ones.

TruthfulQA shows GPT-3 copying human misconceptions, but it does not show imitation causes novel mismatches like churros used in surgery. The 'king of pastiche' line is largely an explanatory metaphor.
The only evidence is a study of how GPT-2-class models store facts. Nothing tests whether embedding-driven substitution causes both GPT-3's good paraphrases and its errors.
No study traces where every piece of GPT output comes from or why it sounds plausible. The GPT-2 novelty study and the InstructGPT training description are only context.
GPT-3 did poorly at tracking entities when tested after training, and forgetting during training was shown only in OLMo. No evidence shows GPT-3's training itself lost entity-property bindings.
